title: The urgent wire request
summary: An email 'from the CEO' asks finance for an urgent EUR 186,000 transfer to a new supplier. Short introductory exercise on business email compromise.

deadlines.label: Ask the bank to recall the transfer, if one was made

nodes.title: Urgent, confidential payment
nodes.body: An email arrives for a finance clerk from the CEO's address: a confidential acquisition needs EUR 186,000 sent today to a new account at a foreign bank. The CEO is travelling and asks her not to phone because the line is not secure.

choices.label: Process the payment, the CEO asked for it personally

insight.text: Urgency, secrecy and 'do not call' are the classic markers. Payments to new accounts need out-of-band verification regardless of who asks.

choices.label: Reply to the email asking the CEO to confirm

insight.text: Confirming through the same channel only asks the attacker to confirm. Use a known phone number or a second approver.

modifiers.text: The reply comes back within minutes: 'Yes, go ahead, it is urgent.' The transfer is released.

choices.label: Call the CEO on her known mobile number to verify before doing anything

insight.text: Out-of-band verification defeats almost all CEO fraud. The CEO knew nothing about it.

nodes.title: The CEO knows nothing
nodes.body: Four hours later the CEO lands and says she never sent the message. The transfer has gone out and the money is already at the foreign bank.

choices.label: Call our bank right now to request a recall and file a police report

insight.text: Recalls work best in the first hours. Banks have a fraud desk for exactly this, and police reports support the claim.

modifiers.text: Because the bank was called within hours, EUR 150,000 is frozen and returned.

choices.label: Handle it on Monday when the right people are back

insight.text: Money moves on within a day. Waiting turns a recoverable loss into a total one.

nodes.title: How did they know?
nodes.body: The attackers knew the CEO's travel dates and the clerk's name. Someone has been reading mail.

choices.label: Review the mailbox, reset credentials, enforce MFA and check for forwarding rules

insight.text: Business email compromise often starts with a phished mailbox and a silent forwarding rule.

choices.label: Delete the suspicious email and move on

insight.text: Deleting the message destroys evidence and leaves the intruder in the mailbox.

choices.label: Mandate call-back verification and dual approval for new or changed payment details

insight.text: A process control removes the dependency on someone noticing the lure under pressure.

choices.label: Send an awareness reminder to all staff

insight.text: Awareness helps but should back a process control, not replace it.
Without a change in process the same message will work on the next clerk.
